title: Sort and Count: Group Objects by Kind, Color and Shape
seo_title: Kindergarten Sorting Worksheets: Sort, Classify and Count Objects
standard_text: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten sorting worksheets: sort objects by kind, color and shape, count each group, find the group with the most or fewest, and spot the one that does not belong. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Put things that are alike in a group. Then count each group.
key_sub: You can sort by kind, color or shape. The biggest number is the most.
body_html:
Sort, then count

To sort means to put things that are alike in the same group. Then count each group.

Ways to sort

Sort byExample
Kindanimals and food
Colorred, blue, yellow
Shapecircles, squares, triangles

Compare the groups

The group with the biggest number has the most. The group with the smallest number has the fewest.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Counting all the thingsCount only the group you are asked about
Counting one thing twiceMark each one as you count
Mixing up color and shapeAsk: am I sorting by color or by shape?

faq.q: What does sort and count mean in kindergarten?
faq.a: Children put objects into groups by kind, color or shape. Then they count how many are in each group and say which group has the most or the fewest.

faq.q: Why is sorting important in math?
faq.a: Sorting teaches children to notice how things are alike and different. It is the first step toward reading graphs and data.

faq.q: How many objects should a kindergartner sort?
faq.a: Each group should have 10 or fewer objects, so children can count them easily.

faq.q: How can I practice sorting at home?
faq.a: Sort laundry by color, toys by kind, or snacks by shape. Ask: How many are in each group? Which group has the most?
